Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the exact visual, structural, and copywriting frameworks required to build high-converting e-commerce emails, including practical tutorials on using Figma to design and slice image-based emails for platforms like Klaviyo or Omnisend. modules: [EML] topics: [email marketing, email design, copywriting, Figma, Klaviyo, Omnisend, conversion rate optimization, email structure, image slicing] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. email structure / positioning the headline, copy, and primary CTA button "above the fold" to capture non-scrollers immediately, followed by a "bridge" section with infographics, and ending with a footer containing category navigation; visual design / creating a seamless, scrolling experience using background gradients and dynamic layouts (e.g., S-curves, GIF carousels) rather than blocky, disjointed sections; skimmable copywriting / optimizing for 3-second attention spans by using punchy headlines, extremely short body copy, bolded main points, and infographics (checklists, icons, timelines) instead of dense paragraphs; AI copywriting workflow / using ChatGPT to reverse-engineer competitor emails by pasting an example, asking for a reusable framework, and prompting it to generate new copy using that specific structure; the "button at the top" rule / the strict design requirement to place a large, easily clickable CTA button immediately below the hero copy, ensuring it is visible without scrolling; footer navigation / utilizing the footer to include "shop by category" buttons (e.g., Men/Women) to capture clicks from users who reached the bottom but did not want the specific product featured in the email; Figma to ESP workflow / the technical process of designing an email in Figma, using the "slice" tool to export sections as individual JPEGs, compressing them (via tools like iLoveIMG), and uploading them as stacked images into an Email Service Provider (ESP); the "hidden text" deliverability hack / placing invisible text (e.g., the brand's "About Us" copy set to size 5, 5% line spacing, and matched to the background color) at the bottom of image-heavy emails to pass spam filters that penalize text-to-image ratios.

The "Button at the Top" Rule: The non-negotiable design principle of placing a massive CTA button immediately below the hero text so that it is fully visible "above the fold" when a user opens the email on mobile.

The Invisible Text Hack: The deliverability tactic of pasting a large block of text (like an "About Us" page) at the bottom of an image-only email, changing the font color to match the background, and shrinking it to trick Gmail's text-to-image spam filters.

The Figma Slicing Workflow: The process of exporting a long email design into multiple smaller image "slices" to optimize load times and allow for multiple, distinct hyperlinks (e.g., splitting a footer into separate slices for different social media icons).

The ChatGPT Reverse-Engineering Prompt: The copywriting strategy of feeding ChatGPT a successful competitor's email, asking it to extract the structural template, and then prompting it to write new copy for your brand using that exact formula.
Skip. Plugs for the creator's agency (Well Copy), the newsletter sign-up pitches, and the extended, repetitive clicks during the live Figma design tutorials unless they illustrate a core concept.
Scope mix. 15% baseline (standard email marketing principles), 85% growth (advanced Figma design, conversion-optimized layouts, and technical deliverability hacks). Volume. ~450 words.
